idiom_name: abstract Component + CustomerCore with map<string, CustomerRole*> + dynamic_cast
implementation_notes: This is the paper's own C++ realization: Customer declares the role protocol (getRole/addRole/removeRole/hasRole by specification), CustomerCore implements it over a specification-keyed container of role pointers, and CustomerRole subclasses forward every Customer operation to the core while adding their own operations; clients ask for a role and recover its concrete type with dynamic_cast. Multiple inheritance of the core and the role interfaces (Fowler's PersonImpHD style) is the alternative when clients should see one fused interface instead of asking for views. A closed role set can instead be stored in std::variant or a discriminated union, but that trades the pattern's runtime extensibility for compile-time exhaustiveness; keep the classic form when roles genuinely come and go at runtime.
pitfalls: Storing roles by value loses the decorator relationship; store owning pointers (unique_ptr) and destroy roles with the core, or role objects leak or dangle.
dynamic_cast needs RTTI and a polymorphic target; builds compiled without RTTI require a different downcast strategy (ids, variant, or a visitor).
Forwarding every Customer operation in CustomerRole duplicates the core interface, so the roles drift when the core changes; keep the shared interface small or generate the forwarding.
